Aspects (abnormal in red) Hila: L higher than R; look for lymphadenopathy and calcifications
claims.quote: H - Hila: L higher than R; lymphadenopathy; calcifications.

claims.text: Simple silicosis: upper lobe predominance of bilateral 1- to 3-mm reticulonodular opacities
claims.quote: In patients with simple silicosis, there is upper lobe predominance of bilateral 1- to 3-mm reticulonodular opacities.

claims.text: Calcified hilar and mediastinal lymph nodes are common and occasionally resemble eggshells; however, eggshell calcification is not pathognomonic for silicosis
claims.quote: Calcified hilar and mediastinal lymph nodes are common and occasionally resemble eggshells; however, eggshell calcification is not pathognomonic for silicosis.

claims.text: Pleural thickening is uncommon unless severe parenchymal disease abuts the pleura
claims.quote: Pleural thickening is uncommon unless a severe parenchymal disease abuts the pleura.

claims.text: Complicated silicosis: large opacities on chest x-ray (conglomerate opacities with calcifications on CT); nodules coalesce as simple silicosis progresses to complicated
claims.quote: Complicated silicosis is characterized by large opacities on chest x-ray or conglomerate opacities with calcifications on chest CT. Imaging shows coalescing of nodules when simple silicosis progresses to complicated silicosis.

claims.text: Chest CT is more sensitive than chest x-ray for detecting silicosis and monitoring progression
claims.quote: Chest CT is more sensitive than chest x-ray for detecting silicosis and monitoring for disease progression.

claims.text: Look-alikes on chest imaging: sarcoidosis, chronic beryllium disease, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, coal worker pneumoconiosis, miliary tuberculosis, fungal pulmonary diseases and metastatic cancer
claims.quote: On chest imaging, a number of disorders can resemble chronic silicosis. They include sarcoidosis, chronic beryllium disease, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, coal worker pneumoconiosis, miliary tuberculosis, fungal pulmonary diseases, and metastatic cancer.

claims.text: Causes Inhalation of respirable crystalline silica dust → nodular pulmonary fibrosis
claims.quote: Silicosis is caused by inhalation of respirable crystalline silica dust and is characterized by nodular pulmonary fibrosis.

claims.text: Associated with increased risk of tuberculosis, COPD, lung cancer and systemic rheumatic disease
claims.quote: Silicosis is associated with increased risk of tuberculosis, COPD, lung cancer, and systemic rheumatic disease.

claims.text: Symptoms Chronic silicosis can be asymptomatic, but many patients develop progressive dyspnea and cough; consolidation, pulmonary hypertension and respiratory failure with or without right ventricular failure may develop in advanced disease
claims.quote: Chronic silicosis can be asymptomatic, but many patients develop progressive dyspnea and cough. Pulmonary consolidation, pulmonary hypertension, and respiratory failure with or without right ventricular failure may develop in advanced disease.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: smoking cessation; ↑ TB risk

claims.text: The cornerstone of treatment is supportive care and, for severe cases, lung transplantation
